sources.note: Legacy-system guidance for plan-making. It now opens by telling authorities preparing a plan under the new system to use the new-system collection instead, which for sites is the four-stage site selection guidance. It is here because an existing land availability assessment is one of the places Stage 1 says to look for sites.

sources.title: Viability: plan-making
sources.note: The plan-making parts only: 'Viability and plan making' and 'Golden Rules for Green Belt development'. It is not specific to either plan-making system and has not been updated for the new one: its paragraph references are to the December 2024 NPPF.

sources.title: Flood risk and coastal change: plan-making
sources.note: The plan-making parts only: taking flood risk into account in preparing plans, the sequential approach and the exception test, without the questions about planning applications. It has not been updated for the new system: it refers to the December 2024 NPPF and to sustainability appraisal. For a new-system plan the August 2026 NPPF's flood policies (F1 to F9 and Annex F) apply.

sources.title: Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004, Part 2: local plans (sections 15B to 15LH)
sources.note: The new local plan sections inserted by section 97 of, and Schedule 7 to, the Levelling-up and Regeneration Act 2023, in force from 25 March 2026. The legacy sections of Part 2 are left out. Sections 15A to 15AI (joint spatial development strategies) and 15K (neighbourhood priorities statements), which these sections refer to, are not shown on legislation.gov.uk.

sources.publisher: legislation.gov.uk (2023 c. 55, revised text valid from 15 July 2026)
sources.title: Levelling-up and Regeneration Act 2023, Part 3 Chapter 2: development plans (sections 92 to 100)
sources.note: Sections 93 (the development plan and national development management policies in decision-making), 95 and 96 are prospective: enacted but not yet in force. Section 94, which says what a national development management policy is, is in force. Section 97 brings in Schedule 7, whose text is in the PCPA 2004 sections above.
